series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Attach the same quadratic-mean (QM) Bollinger-style signal once per timeframe (H1, H4, D1). Each TF votes bullish/bearish from how far close sits relative to the QM/QM' band baseline (or from upper/lower band crosses). Combine votes by optimized signal weights into one open/close decision. Intended MTF use: slower TF as macro-trend probability, faster TF as crossover trigger.
data_needed: close prices on each assigned TF
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURJPY; chart H1 with parallel H1/H4/D1 signals; year 2023
why_new_for_mis: Treats multi-timeframe disagreement/alignment as an explicit weighted sensing panel rather than a single-chart indicator, with QM high-bias and QM' low-bias envelopes as the band generators.
quote: Multi-time frame strategies can be a boon in instances such as when looking for divergence opportunities between the tracked time frames such as a short-term bearish trend in the faster (or shorter time frame) could be a major signal if this is taking place in the backdrop of a major bullish trend in the larger time frame.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Quadratic/root-mean-square mean biases toward larger values in a positive-only set: QM=sqrt(mean(x^2)). Mirror QM'=AM+(AM-QM) biases toward smaller values. Pair as high/low buffers for envelopes or divergence signals, continuing the prior Pythagorean-means envelope pattern.
data_needed: positive-valued price sample of length n
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an RMS-biased upper envelope and mirrored lower envelope without assuming Gaussian bands, useful as an alternate width/regime band family.
quote: Like most non-arithmetic mean averages, they do have a bias or preference weighting and this, unlike the Geometric mean and the Harmonic mean, is towards the larger values in the set.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Estimate Hurst H via rescaled-range: split sample into non-overlapping segments of size t=2..n/2, mean-adjust, cumulate deviations, log(R/S) vs log(t), linear-regression slope = H. If H>0.5 (persistence) compare bid to slow MA for trend-follow; if H<0.5 (anti-persistence) compare bid to fast MA for mean-reversion. Sample length = fast+slow periods.
why_new_for_mis: Uses rolling R/S Hurst as an explicit trend-vs-range regime switch that selects which MA horizon and which side of price-vs-MA logic is active.
quote: we'd calculate the Hurst exponent to determine if the market is trending (which would typically give us a value greater than 0.5) or if the market is mean-reverting/ whipsawed (that would give us a value less than 0.5).

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Same R/S log-log fit yields intercept C alongside slope H. Equal H but different C across instruments implies similar persistence with different swing amplitude; article treats C as a volatility/risk-profile proxy for position-sizing regimes.
data_needed: same R/S regression that yields H
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Illustrated with equities comparison; EA tested on GBPCHF H4 2023
why_new_for_mis: Separates persistence class (H) from amplitude/risk class (C) as two independent sensing coordinates from one R/S fit.
quote: the C-constant could be understood as a proxy for volatility.;;The equities with a higher C-constant would have wider price swings across its averages unlike the equity with a smaller C-constant.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Control sensor without Hurst: CorrCoef of two adjacent slow-period close windows; if >= threshold use slow MA trend-follow (price above/below mean). Else CorrCoef on fast-period windows; if <= -threshold use fast MA mean-reversion. Lighter substitute for R/S persistence gating.
data_needed: close windows of length slow and fast
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPCHF H4; 2023 (outperformed Hurst EA in article runs)
why_new_for_mis: Direct lagged autocorrelation at two horizons as a cheap persistence/anti-persistence regime gate without rescaled-range regression.
quote: first assesses for any positive correlations over the longer (slower) averaging period. If there is any such positive correlation then the moving average over this slower period is used to assess for trend following setups

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Reject raw arctan(ΔMA/N_bars) because angle depends on price scale and chart TF. Instead measure height = DM(t)-DM(t+L) on a decaying moving average, and set base = max(point, range of DM over the prior length-L window). Angle = ±(180/π)·arctan(|height|/base). Yields comparable degrees across FX decimals and timeframes.
why_new_for_mis: Converts trend steepness into a scale- and timeframe-stable angle by expressing the time axis in units of recent price range—usable as a cross-instrument momentum/steepness sensor.
quote: When presented with any two price points that are at a distance D apart in time, the distance D will be converted to the price units of the range in price over the previous distance D before it.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Decaying MA weights recent prices with 1/2^(n-i). Signal fires only when signed attack angle is inside a critical band [threshold, threshold+band] (or negative mirror)—borrowed from aerodynamic critical angle of attack—rather than any angle beyond a single threshold. Vote strength = |angle|/90 scaled to 0–100.
why_new_for_mis: Senses a usable trend-steepness regime as an angle band (not merely 'steep enough'), filtering both flat and excessively steep DMA slopes.
quote: the critical angle of attack introduces the notion that this angle, on which we base our opening decisions, rather than being defined by a solo threshold value is actually better defined to be within a band or specific range.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Simple 5-8-1 GAN: generator emits a direction/score; long only if discriminator backs the sample and gen_out>0.5; short if backed and gen_out<0.5. Article varies learning-rate schedules (fixed, step/exp/poly/inverse-time decay, cosine annealing, cyclical) as the training path to those weights—sensor semantics stay generator+discriminator agreement.
why_new_for_mis: Neural direction sensor that requires adversarial discriminator confirmation before a generator forecast counts as a market read—distinct from a lone MLP score.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: 3-layer MLP (5-8-1) with Sigmoid activations forecasts next close from recent raw closes. LongCondition if forecast>bid, ShortCondition if forecast<bid; result is forecast's percentile within the recent input price window rescaled to 0–100. Adaptive LRs (Adagrad, RMSProp, ADAM/ME, AdaDelta) and one-cycle schedule are training variants, not alternate sensors.
data_needed: recent close window of size MLP inputs
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: NZDUSD daily (prices in 0–1 for 2023 so Sigmoid-compatible without batch-norm); 2023
why_new_for_mis: Maps a next-close neural forecast into a window-relative strength score rather than a raw price, usable as a calibrated neural change sensor.
quote: we simply compare the projected price to the array of input prices and come up with a percentile double value. We convert this percentile value into an integer in the expected 0 to 100

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Before each MLP layer, normalize activations then apply learnable y=γx+β. Feature-scaling (min-max→[0,1]) paired with Hard-Sigmoid/Sigmoid/Softmax; Robust-scaling ((x-median)/IQR, outliers can exceed ±1) paired with Softsign/TANH—recommended for noisy/volatile price buffers; Standard/Z-score unbound and riskier. Control runs without normalization.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURJPY daily; 2023; feature+sigmoid and robust+softsign tested
why_new_for_mis: Gives a concrete recipe for feeding volatile FX prices into neural sensors without exploding gradients: robust/IQR scaling when outliers matter, feature scaling when outputs must stay in [0,1].
quote: Noisy data or datasets with a lot of outliers, which from a trader’s perspective could include price buffers of very volatile securities, are all ideal data sets to use with robust scaling and TANH activation.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Two MLP sensors: (1) regressor 4-7-1 on recent price-change percentages with TANH + Huber loss → signed next change; (2) classifier 3-6-3 on past 3 bar class labels with Softmax-compatible CCE → 3-way probability over down/flat/up; long if P_up dominates, short if P_down dominates. Loss choice (MSE/MAE/Huber vs BCE/CCE) follows regressor vs classifier role.
data_needed: percent price changes or discrete bar classes
why_new_for_mis: Splits neural sensing into continuous next-change regression versus discrete short-horizon regime classification with loss/activation pairs that keep gradients usable.
quote: Classification networks are purposed to forecast discrete class labels from a pool of predefined possible categories. These networks output probabilities indicating the likelihood of each class

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Add regularization term to loss via matrix norms of weights: L1/Lasso (prefer P1 norm) promotes sparsity—paired with Softmax/Sigmoid + CCE/BCE for classifier MLPs; L2/Ridge (Frobenius/P2) smooths weights—paired with Softsign + Huber for regressors. Dropout and Elastic-Net also coded. Same EURUSD daily 2023 regressor/classifier setups as prior loss article.
why_new_for_mis: Operational rule for stabilizing neural market sensors: sparse L1 for class-probability heads, smooth L2 for continuous change heads—reduces over-fit of the sensing network to in-sample noise.
quote: If we were to use L1 Lasso for instance, by penalizing with just the absolute value of the weights, the training process tends to reduce a lot of the weights in the network layers to zero while leaving only the critical ones

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Unconventional 8→4 RBM trained with reconstruction error + backpropagation (positive phase visible→hidden, negative phase hidden→reconstructed visible using same weights). Hidden vector is a dimensionality-reduced 'price embedding' of recent close changes, then fed to a regressor MLP (soft-sign + Huber) that forecasts next change. Concurrent RBM+MLP training on each bar.
data_needed: recent close-change windows for RBM visible layer
labels of subsequent changes for MLP
why_new_for_mis: Inserts an unsupervised compressed embedding of price changes before the forecasting head—analogous to word embedding—so the neural sensor reads relational structure rather than raw deltas alone.
quote: by default, security price data (Even though numeric) cannot be easily ‘understood’ by neural networks off the bat. And our approach for making this more understandable is by using a backpropagation trained RBM.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Train MLP next-close-change forecaster with SVR-style loss: zero penalty when |output-label|≤ε, else C·|error|, plus 0.5·||W||_P2. Ignores small noise inside the ε-tube while still regressing continuous targets. Contrasted with GPR as better for stable/staple-like series.
why_new_for_mis: Neural change sensor whose training ignores sub-ε noise—useful when MIS wants trend-level forecasts without fitting tick-scale jitter.
quote: SVR introduces a loss-insensitive parameter epsilon that sees to it that errors with a magnitude less than epsilon are ignored and do not result in weights or parameter adjustments

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Separate trailing MLP: inputs are changes of (high−low) bar ranges; target is next change in that range series. Positive forecasted range-change ⇒ rising volatility ⇒ tighten/move stop in proportion to projected increase (article notes the opposite policy is also debatable).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDJPY daily; 2023 with and without trailing class
why_new_for_mis: Dedicated neural sensor of bar-range expansion/contraction as a volatility-change read, separate from directional close-change forecasting.
quote: we need to find out what the next change in price bar range change is going to be. ... if the projected change in price bar range is positive, implying volatility is increasing, we make steps to move our stop loss in proportion to our projected increase.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Build a 3×3 environment from short-horizon vs long-horizon (scale×short) signed price changes: each axis ∈ {bearish, flat, bullish} → 9 states. Q-map stores scores for actions {sell, flat, buy}. CriticReward normalizes floating P&L into [0,1]; CriticState updates Q via off-policy Q-learning. MLP classifier 2-8-3 takes (row,col) state coords and matches Q action distribution; optional Markov 9×9 transition matrix weights the Q update by P(old→new).
data_needed: close changes over 1 bar and over m_scale bars
optional Markov on state index series
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GBPJPY daily; 2023; tests with and without Markov weighting
why_new_for_mis: Explicit dual-horizon bull/flat/bear grid as a discrete market-regime state, with Q-learning (+ optional Markov transitions) teaching which action distribution belongs to each cell—usable as a regime sensor feeding a classifier head.
quote: if we focus on 3 basic metrics namely bullishness, bearishness, and flatness, then each of these three can have indicators on a shorter time frame and a longer time frame. So, in essence our ‘environment’ is a 9-index space (3 x 3 for short-term by long-term)

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Single CiBands signal class with up to 8 pattern detectors (bitmask m_patterns_used 0–255), each with optimizable 0–100 weight. Patterns covered here: (0) close cross back inside outer band; (1) single bounce off outer band; (2) one-bar squeeze (upper dips and lower rises together) then close at outer band; (3) double bottom/top near outer band; (4) bounce off middle band as trend continuation; (5) 3-bar shrinking bar-range 'volume' proxy while close hugs outer band (exhaustion). Patterns 6–7 deferred.
data_needed: optional bar range as volume proxy
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: USDCHF daily; 2023; each pattern tested solo
why_new_for_mis: Turns Bollinger width/location into a multi-event sensing panel (squeeze, exhaustion via range divergence, mid-band continuation, outer-band rejection) selectable by bitmask rather than a single band-touch rule.
quote: The Bollinger Bands squeeze occurs when the upper and lower band are very close to each other for a given stretch of time such that volatility is low and the potential for breakout opportunities is imminent.

series_key: mql5 wizard techniques you should know
mechanism: Where true FX volume is unreliable, use price-bar range as volume proxy. Pattern 5: Range(t)<Range(t+1)<Range(t+2) while close is nearer the lower (buy) or upper (sell) band than the middle—read as volume/participation drying up at an extreme (exhaustion/reversal).
why_new_for_mis: Liquidity/participation proxy from bar-range contraction co-located with Bollinger extremes—usable when tick volume is broker-dependent.
quote: when tracking or measuring volume in implementing this we use, arguably, the next best proxy. Price bar range.
